Veteran engineers are called quitters who won’t adapt. The data says they’re pushed out. And the junior jobs are vanishing at the same time.

6 min read
Just now

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image by Ahmed M. AbdelfattahOlder tech workers are being cast as quitters who won’t learn AI. The data tells a harder story, and read next to the collapse of entry-level hiring, it points at something worse than either trend alone.
A few weeks ago I wrote about the disappearance of the entry-level software job. How the tasks that used to train junior developers are exactly the ones AI now absorbs.
How the bottom rung of the career ladder, the one I’m about to step onto as a computer science graduate, is being quietly removed.
This week a companion story surfaced. And it’s about the top of the same ladder.
Across the tech industry, older engineers are leaving early. Fortune, the Wall Street Journal, and the Seattle Times have all documented the same pattern.
Veteran workers in their late 50s and early 60s, many with three decades of experience, stepping away rather than rebuild their careers around AI.
The easy version of this story is that these are people who won’t adapt. Who find AI…
